title: D2 error codes spec (canonical generalized schema)
description: Canonical generalized schema for every *-error-codes spec file - the source-of-truth catalogs the unified error-codes generator reads to emit <Domain>ErrorCodes.g.cs and <Domain>Failures.g.cs (.NET) and <domain>-error-codes.g.ts and <domain>-failures.g.ts (TypeScript) for each domain. The generic cross-cutting spec (contracts/error-codes/error-codes.spec.json) and every per-domain spec (contracts/<domain>-error-codes/<domain>-error-codes.spec.json) conform to this shape, and a per-domain schema.json either copies this definition verbatim or $refs it. Every code carries an owner prefix and, outside the generic catalog, a domain token: GEN_{REST} for a generic or framework code, LIB_{DOMAIN}_{REST} for a library catalog, DOM_{DOMAIN}_{REST} for an application-domain catalog. The generator enforces the whole prefix as one string - the catalog configuration names it, a code that does not start with it fails the build with D2ERC001 - and derives the emitted class names from the spec filename. The merged registry hard-fails on a code collision across catalogs. Example spec entry: { "code": "LIB_PAGINATION_REQUEST_REQUIRED", "httpStatus": 400, "category": "validation_failure", "userMessageKey": "TK.Common.Pagination.REQUEST_REQUIRED", "factoryName": "RequestRequired", "factoryShape": "standard", "doc": "No page request was supplied." }

code.description: Wire-format error code (SCREAMING_SNAKE). Shape-only regex - each catalog enforces its own full owner prefix, GEN_ or LIB_{DOMAIN}_ or DOM_{DOMAIN}_, and a code that does not carry it fails the build with D2ERC001. Must be unique across the spec.

httpStatus.description: HTTP status mapping for transport. In a per-domain catalog it selects the base D2Result factory a <Domain>Failures factory delegates to (404 -> NotFound, 409 -> Conflict, 400 -> ValidationFailed, 401 -> Unauthorized, 403 -> Forbidden, 503 -> ServiceUnavailable, 500 -> UnhandledException, 413 -> PayloadTooLarge, 429 -> TooManyRequests). In the generic catalog each code defines its own named factory (see factoryName); multiple codes may share a status (e.g. VALIDATION_FAILED and CANCELED are both 400 but are distinct factories), so the emitted factory is identified by factoryName + factoryShape, not status alone. Expanding the supported set requires extending this enum and the generator's status validation.

category.description: Closed semantic/telemetry classification. NOT the factory selector - httpStatus drives factory selection. Added to the wire (gRPC trailers + JSON envelope) so consumers can do generic class-based handling (e.g. retry any infrastructure_unavailable) without importing the producer's catalog. partial_success classifies the read-partial SOME_FOUND and write-partial PARTIAL_SUCCESS codes - a mixed per-target outcome. Both are failures: anything short of every item or every target is reported as one, and a caller that may accept a partial outcome opts in by testing the code.

userMessageKey.description: Translation key reference rendered as the messages argument on the emitted D2Result factory (e.g. TK.Auth.Errors.UNAUTHORIZED, TK.Common.Errors.NOT_FOUND). Written as the C# symbol-path string - the .NET emitter uses it verbatim in the factory body; the TS emitter passes it to tk(...). The generator enforces existence by inverse-transforming the symbol path to the snake_case key (TK.Auth.Errors.UNAUTHORIZED -> auth_errors_UNAUTHORIZED) and asserting membership in contracts/messages/en-US.json. Coarse on purpose for auth-class codes - one key per status bucket so the user-facing surface does not leak which validation step failed.

factoryName.description: PascalCase symbol for the emitted factory method on <Domain>Failures (e.g. BearerMissing, JwksUnavailable, SubdivisionNotFound). The .NET emitter uses it as-is; the TS emitter lowercases the first character to camelCase (bearerMissing). Must be unique across the spec.

factoryShape.description: Closed enum that drives the generated factory's signature variant. standard: the one universal error-factory shape (messages?, inputErrors?, errorCode?, category?, traceId?) - ALL optional. Every error factory at any status can stamp a domain code + category and optionally carry inputErrors; the errorCode / category overrides are how a delegating domain factory stamps a specific code + category on a base status. none: no factory generated for this code; only the constant + boolean are emitted - used by codes with no current factory (e.g. SOME_FOUND/PARTIAL_SUCCESS whose data-carrying factories stay hand-rolled, IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT/serialization codes).

doc.description: XML <summary> text rendered on the emitted constant + factory (.NET) and JSDoc text on the emitted TS constant + factory.

deprecated.description: When true, the entry is deprecated: the generated C# constant + factory carry [Obsolete] and the TS constant + factory carry @deprecated. Additive - the entry is NEVER deleted. Deleting a deprecated (or non-deprecated) entry is a breaking change the JSON-diff gate fails.

deprecatedReason.description: Plain dev-facing English explaining why the code is deprecated; rendered into the [Obsolete("...")] message, the @deprecated JSDoc, and the changelog entry. NOT a TK key (developer-facing, not user-facing).

replacedBy.description: Wire code of the successor entry (e.g. RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND). Must reference a real, non-deprecated entry in the merged registry. Omit for pure retirement with no replacement.

sunset.description: ISO-8601 date for the RFC 8594 Sunset response header. A host whose response pipeline emits that header reads the date from here; a host that does not ignores it.
